newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps drift sideways, Brent CFDs quiet.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps drift sideways, Brent CFDs quiet.

text.p: European oil swaps were listless on Thursday with levels steady or a touch firmer. Dealers said activity was off compared with previous days this week.
Brent CFDs held steady around -66 cents under August Brent for June 16-20 while June 23-27 was unchanged at -54/55 cents and June 30-July 4 was put around -48/49 cents under.
A strong morning bid for dated Brent had led to initial expectations that CFDs would rise, but with the bid failing to connect with an offer the market remained unruffled.
Heavy fuel swaps were heard traded around $84.50 for June while July was still backwardated and valued at $84. Dealers put 3Q around $84.50, much the same level as August.
Low sulphur swaps had a quiet day with June pegged around $91.50 and July about 25 cents stronger. Two 3,000 tonne barges were sold at $94.50 fob Flushing.

A perceived squeeze in the physical gasoline market which has tightened barges has also thinned activity on the swaps side. Dealers said little had traded but June was bid around $188 and July at $183.
Naphtha was dogged by poor interest with July pegged around $178.50 and August fairly close. The balance of June was placed at $181.75, but most of June's interest was against July.
